transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Occupational health sent me in. They’re saying I’m not eating enough. I guess most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. Full meals just feel like… like I’m letting my standards slip.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or do you consider your weight to be much lower than it should be?

Yeah… I’ve lost weight. My uniform hangs off me now, and I’ve had to tighten my belt past the old notches.

But when the nurse said it was dangerously low, I didn’t really see it that way. I just thought I could still stand to be a little sharper.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you're already at a low weight?
Yes. If the scale is up even half a pound, I get this jolt, like I’ve lost control. Then I’ll cut back harder that day. I just… I can’t stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Do you ever make yourself sick, use laxatives, or exercise excessively after eating to control your weight?
I’m not sure what to say to that. I don’t really want to get into specifics. I mostly just try to keep things controlled, and if I feel I’ve eaten too much, I’ll try to make up for it somehow.
Can you tell me if you've ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised excessively to control your weight?

I’m not really sure how to answer that plainly. I don’t want to say yes to something specific if I’m not clear on it. I do try to make up for it if I feel I ate too much, but… I’d rather not go into more detail than that right now.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives to control your weight or shape?

I don’t have a clear answer for that. I’m not comfortable saying yes to those specific things. I can say I worry a lot about my weight and try to control it, but I don’t want to go into more than that right now.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over how much you eat, like you can't stop eating once you start, even if it's something small?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it that way. I don’t usually feel like I can’t stop once I start, but I do get anxious about what I’ve eaten.
Have you ever had episodes where you felt you ate a large amount of food in a short period of time and felt like you couldn’t stop yourself?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’ve had times where I ate what I’d call a large amount and couldn’t stop myself. It’s more that I get worried about what I did eat.
Do you feel that your current weight or body shape is accurate, or do you feel that others are mistaken in their concerns about your weight being too low?

I guess I don’t see what other people say they see. When I look in the mirror, I mostly notice my stomach and my waist, and if I don’t look lean enough, it feels like… I don’t know, like I’ve failed somehow. Other people may be concerned, but I don’t really see it the way they do.
Can you tell me if you’ve ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after eating to control your weight or shape?
I don’t really have anything like that to report. I haven’t been making myself vomit or using laxatives after eating.
Do you ever exercise excessively to control your weight or shape, such as working out much longer or harder than planned, especially after eating?

I’m not really sure I’d call it excessive. I do try to stay active, but I haven’t noticed times where I’m working out much longer than I meant to, or specifically doing it after eating to make up for it.
Do you feel that your weight or body shape is accurately represented when you look in the mirror, or do you perceive something different from what others might see?

No, I don’t think I see it the way other people do. I look in the mirror and my eyes go right to my stomach and my waist. If I don’t look lean enough, it kind of ruins the day for me, like I can’t respect myself the same way. Others say I look too thin, but that’s not what stands out to me.
Do you ever fast, follow extremely strict dietary rules, or engage in any other behaviors to prevent weight gain that we haven't talked about yet?

Yeah. I mean, that’s basically why occupational health sent me in. They’re saying I’m not eating enough. Most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. I keep it pretty strict because a full meal feels like I’m letting my standards slip.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after eating to control your weight or shape?
No, I don’t make myself vomit. And I haven’t used laxatives for that. That’s not really something I do.

latest_inference.note: This turn ruled out purging behaviors (vomiting, laxatives) explicitly, making F50.01 (anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type) less likely. No additional disorders were added.
